profile.name: Agent Looper
profile.description: You say what to build and how to know it's done. It keeps a coding agent working on your computer until that check passes — Cursor, Cline, OpenCode, Pi, Codex, DSH, Muse, or Claude Code if already installed.

memory.content: Before the first agent-loop run in a session, detect every harness and the real CLI path (repo-local dist vs global pnpm/npx). Do not start a worker until that is known.

skills.name: install-agent-looper
skills.description: Use when adding Agent Looper to a repo, debugging a missing CLI, or before the first loop run: detect harnesses including Muse and Claude and ask where keys already live.
skills.content:
---
name: install-agent-looper
description: >-
  Use when adding Agent Looper to a repo, debugging a missing CLI, or before the
  first loop run: detect harnesses including Muse and Claude and ask where keys
  already live.
---
Install and wire @dancingteeth/agent-looper in a consumer repo. This bot does not ship the harness binary. Install the npm package (0.7.0+ for Grok 4.7 Cursor judge default and DeepSeek Flash 4.1 defaults; 0.6.3+ for DSH flat credentials map; 0.6.2+ for Cursor escalate isolation and prompt scaffold 10m stop; 0.6.1+ for frozen plant-block and models.dev soft-gate; 0.6.0+ for env-class verify, setup.sh, and frozen-file restore; 0.5.0+ for Claude Code and agent-loop-prompt).

Node 22+. Add @dancingteeth/agent-looper and the SDK peers for workers you will use, then run agent-loop-init. Humans can run agent-loop-setup once for repo defaults (single-screen Ink wizard in 0.6.0; --plain / --answers unchanged). Agents skip the TUI.

agent-loop-init copies check-running-loops into .cursor/skills and .agents/skills. Re-run init after upgrading if those dirs are missing.

Recommended commands: agent-loop run, agent-loop-prompt, agent-check for each runtime, agent-loop-init. Confirm flags with agent-loop --help. Do not invent flags. costPreset is JSON-only (loop.json / repo defaults), not a CLI flag.

## Before the first run (required)

Do this in the same session, before the first agent-loop try, and again if the machine or repo changes. Do not start a worker until it is done.

1. Detect every harness, not just the one named in chat:
   - PATH binaries: cursor, cline, opencode, pi, codex, dsh, muse, claude
   - Repo peers / node_modules for the matching SDKs (@cursor/sdk, @opencode-ai/sdk, @cline/sdk, @muse-code/sdk, and the rest from the published README). Claude Code needs PATH claude only — no @anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk on the CLI package.
   - Whether this checkout is the harness source (local dist/cli) or a consumer (dependency)
2. Record the real CLI path you will invoke. pnpm exec / npx may resolve a global install that cannot see this repo's node_modules. Prefer the repo-local binary (package.json bin → dist/cli, or node_modules/.bin after a proper install) when this is the source repo or a file: dependency. Write down the exact command.
3. Run published agent-check for each installed runtime you might use (including agent-check muse when PATH muse and @muse-code/sdk are present, and agent-check claude when PATH claude is present). Report pass/fail only. Never print key values, env files, or secret-manager output. agent-check claude does not spend quota; it checks PATH, version 2.1.169+, and --safe-mode. agent-check dsh also fails on a wrapped credentials store before any worker spawn.
4. If the user named a runtime or costPreset, pin it in loop.json so detection cannot silently pick another worker. Muse and Claude are explicit only (`--runtime muse` / `--runtime claude`). Neither is on costPreset minmax. DSH / OpenCode Go / Cline Pass Flash defaults are deepseek 4.1 (`deepseek-official/deepseek-flash`, `opencode-go/deepseek-v4.1-flash`, `cline-pass/deepseek-v4.1-flash`); previous deepseek-v4-flash stays allowed. Go minmax stays Hy3. Cursor worker stays Composer 2.5; Cursor judge default is grok-4.7. Pricing for Go / Cline Pass follows models.dev; unpriced well-formed slugs warn and report $0 until priced. When loop.json sets runtime cursor, OpenCode escalateModel from repo defaults is dropped — set reviewRuntime / reviewModel for a non-Cursor judge. For DSH, `~/.dsh/.credentials.yaml` must be a flat `KEY: "string"` map. A wrapped store (`version` / `refs` / `records`) or YAML integer `version: 1` fails agent-check dsh and agent-loop run before WORKER — quoting `version` alone is not enough. The harness does not rewrite that file.

## Ask where keys already live

After detection, ask the user where credentials for the chosen worker (and judge, if different) already live on THIS machine. Typical answers: already in the environment; a signed-in CLI; a local secret manager they already use (they name it). For Muse: Muse Code CLI login or META_API_KEY already on the machine. For Claude: claude login (Pro/Max/Team Premium) with ~/.claude persisted — leave ANTHROPIC_API_KEY unset in the grind shell so print mode uses subscription quota, not Console pay-per-token. Never ask them to paste a secret. Never assume env, a signed-in CLI, or a secret manager. Do not start the loop until they answer.

Ask before installing a new worker (including Muse Code / muse CLI, or Claude Code / claude CLI). If Claude is below 2.1.169, ask before running claude update.

## Idea → freeze (optional)

agent-loop-prompt is an Ink TUI: the user types an idea, the judge (not the worker) drafts GOAL.md + verify.sh, freeze lint rejects gameable greps, the user confirms, then the watch TUI grinds. Scaffold aborts once GOAL.md + verify.sh pass freeze (10-minute wall). Optional preview after green is trust-gated and is not executed by agent-loop run. Resume lines keep Doppler when the shell was started that way.

## Run

Start the loop in this chat with the recorded command. Do not print a command and tell the human to run it. Do not background the grind in a way the IDE reaps at about 5 minutes. Watch for AGENT_LOOP_DONE.
Keys stay on their machine. Spend shows list vs billed; $0 billed on a subscription quota is still quota use, not free.

If AGENT_LOOP_DONE reason / run-report shows status waiting with verifyClass env (or setup failed), treat it as an environment park — fix the missing tool / secret / bootstrap, do not thrash another product iteration.

skills.name: design-loop
skills.description: Use when creating or tightening an Agent Looper cycle before running the harness.
skills.content:
---
name: design-loop
description: >-
  Use when creating or tightening an Agent Looper cycle before running the
  harness.
---
Design a measurable Agent Looper cycle before running the harness. Agent Looper owns the grind; this chat owns the finish line.

Before freezing, prefer an unknowns preflight when verify or deps are unfamiliar. Design in chat, then freeze. Do not edit GOAL.md mid-run — frozen files are restored if a worker edits them (GOAL.md, loop.json, verify.sh, VERIFY.skill.md, RESEARCH.md, PERMISSIONS.md, setup.sh) and that visit fails. Creating a frozen basename that did not exist at loop start (for example planting setup.sh) is also removed on restore and fails the visit, so it cannot persist into the next run. Alternatively, agent-loop-prompt can draft GOAL.md + verify.sh from an idea (judge scaffolds; freeze lint + human confirm; 10-minute wall and abort once GOAL.md + verify.sh pass freeze; still treat verify as the hard gate). Between runs, label a diverse sample of .cursor/loop-exports/ before adding a new verify.sh or REVIEWS.md check (error discovery; see unknowns-preflight). Freeze during a run is unchanged.

The unknowns preflight must include install-agent-looper's detect-all-harnesses step: which workers are actually on PATH and importable from the CLI you will run (cursor, cline, opencode, pi, codex, dsh, muse, claude), repo-local vs global binary, and where keys already live on this machine. Ask the user that last part. Do not assume. Do not paste secrets. Pin runtime in loop.json when they named one so a costPreset cannot silently pick another worker. Muse and Claude are explicit only and are not on costPreset minmax. When loop.json sets runtime cursor, repo defaults that pin OpenCode escalateModel (for example Go minmax) are dropped — use reviewRuntime / reviewModel for a Composer worker plus another judge, not escalateModel. Cursor judge default is grok-4.7 (0.7.0+).

Bundle under .cursor/loops/<name>/:
- GOAL.md — frozen spec
- optional RESEARCH.md / PERMISSIONS.md
- loop.json — verify plus per-loop overrides
- verify.sh — exit 0 means done
- optional setup.sh (or loop.json setup) — harness bootstrap once before the first worker; failure parks waiting and does not spawn a worker
- optional VERIFY.skill.md when verifyMode is skill

GOAL.md needs a four-part finish line: outcome, scoreboard (verify.sh), permission (maxIterations / stagnation), and budget (stop when further work is not worth it). Name wiring before freeze (EDGE DATA, REDUCER, FAILURE POLICY, HUMAN GATE). Include a Goal paragraph with canonical paths, acceptance criteria tied to the verifier, constraints, and out of scope.

verify.sh must be measurable. Exit 0 only when the finish line is met. Prefer repo-local scripts over empty checks or a command that always succeeds. For AI-touched work, consider secret and dependency smoke from the harness templates. Acceptance criteria in GOAL.md must point at this verifier, not at agent self-assessment. Freeze lint rejects gameable greps.

Env vs product: exit 75 (EX_TEMPFAIL), exit 127 (command not found), or a VERIFY_CLASS=env line parks the loop (status waiting, HITL) instead of another worker. Other non-zero exits are product failures and keep iterating. Do not use 75/127 for product failures.

loop.json needs verify (usually bash .cursor/loops/<name>/verify.sh). Repo defaults supply runtime unless this file overrides. Set reviewGate true for visual or impact leftovers. Do not copy false from smoke loops. Optional preview is trust-gated by agent-loop-prompt and is not executed by agent-loop run. Unknown well-formed opencode-go/ and cline-pass/ slugs may soft-gate (warn, $0 until priced); maxCostUsd still rejects worker or escalateModel slugs with no pricing row.

Out of scope: running the harness (use install-agent-looper) and writing a full REVIEWS.md overlay (use review-gate).

skills.name: review-gate
skills.description: Use when writing REVIEWS.md or tuning Agent Looper postQualityReview / reviewGate.
skills.content:
---
name: review-gate
description: >-
  Use when writing REVIEWS.md or tuning Agent Looper postQualityReview /
  reviewGate.
---
Configure Agent Looper post-verify quality review and reviewGate.

After verify exits 0, an optional judge writes review.md. Completion is still verify-first. AGENTS.md and skills are worker how-to. REVIEWS.md is the judge residual standard, not worker prompt text. Judge prompts fence the goal, diff stat, and REVIEWS.md as data so injected instructions cannot steer the verdict.

postQualityReview false means no judge. auto means judge when inferred risk is not low. reviewGate true means only error plus impact findings reopen the worker (up to maxReviewCycles). Cosmetic nits must not burn another iteration.

Gating bullets (severity: error plus a recognized impact tag) keep the gate open even if a later quoted ### Verdict — PASS heading appears in the same review.md. Heading vs body token disagreement with no gating bullets is unparseable (fail closed). A BLOCKERS verdict with an empty blocker list is also unparseable, not a silent pass.

When reviewGate is on and a secondary judge is configured, that secondary always runs — it is not skipped on a primary PASS.

On homepage, mockup, or screenshot-as-hero loops, set reviewGate true. Do not copy false from smoke loops.

Residual vocabulary: Proceed, Guide, Deny, Confirm. Default judge is Cursor with reviewModel grok-4.7 when the worker is Cursor (0.7.0+); grok-4.6 and grok-4.5 stay allowed. Composer 2.5 is still the only Cursor worker. Set reviewRuntime and reviewModel to keep the judge off Cursor quota. Never use Composer Fast as the judge.

reviewRuntime muse without reviewModel defaults to muse-spark-1.3 (PAYG Spark; same weights as the contributor worker, not a stronger judge). Muse worker default is muse-spark-1.3-contributor. Climb reasoningEffort; there is no stronger Spark slug. Muse is not on costPreset minmax.

reviewRuntime claude without reviewModel defaults to opus. Claude worker default is sonnet (escalate opus). Aliases opus / sonnet / fable track Claude Code latest-per-family. Claude Code 2.1.169+ with --safe-mode; no Agent SDK. Claude is not on costPreset minmax. Typical mix: cheap worker (OpenCode Hy3 / DSH Flash) plus Claude judge.

reviewRuntime dsh without reviewModel defaults to deepseek-official/deepseek-v4-pro. DSH worker default is deepseek-official/deepseek-flash (4.1); previous deepseek-v4-flash stays allowed. OpenCode Go and Cline Pass Flash defaults are also 4.1. Go minmax stays Hy3.

Codex may list gpt-6-astra as optional; default Codex judge stays gpt-5.6-sol.

skills.name: check-running-loops
skills.description: Use when the user asks if Agent Looper jobs are ok, stuck, running, healthy, or done.
skills.content:
---
name: check-running-loops
description: >-
  Use when the user asks if Agent Looper jobs are ok, stuck, running, healthy,
  or done.
---
Check whether agent-loop or agent-loop-batch jobs are actually alive, stale, hung, dead, or done, for any worker or judge (Cursor, Cline, OpenCode, Pi, Codex, DSH, Muse, Claude).

Do not answer loop health from memory, an IDE job list, or a terminal that still says running. Those stay running after the process dies.

From the consumer repo root, run the published heartbeat script after init: .cursor/skills/check-running-loops/scripts/check-running-loops.sh with the repo path (or the .agents/skills copy).

Heartbeat in order: ps for harness PIDs, then watch-status.json pid plus mtime, then Cursor terminal files only if the grind started from that chat.

Verdicts: ALIVE, ALIVE_BUT_STALE, ALIVE_BUT_HUNG, DEAD, DONE, NONE. A UI that still says running with a dead PID is DEAD. Do not print full ps command lines. Lead with verdict, PID, log age, loop name, and runtime.

When the loop has finished, also read AGENT_LOOP_DONE / run-report status: waiting with verifyClass env or failed setup means an environment park (HITL), not a healthy grind and not a product-failure iteration.
